iOS 27 will focus on bug fixes and performance improvements for apps like Safari, Mail, and Calendar.

In the Messages app, iOS 27 fixes what I consider to be the three most annoying bugs…The update will roll out to all users in a few weeks.

iOS 27: Three major Messages bug fixes

First, Apple says iOS 27 will automatically retry failed messages. I've had this experience countless times: I tap send on a message, then immediately swipe up to return to my iPhone's Home Screen, only to later discover that the message I thought had been sent was never actually delivered.

On iOS 26 and earlier, users had to go back into the Messages app and manually tap the 'Retry' button next to the affected message. But in iOS 27, the system will automatically retry sending in the background.

Second, Apple says iOS 27 lets users send a continuous stream of photos, videos, and text messages in Messages. This fix addresses a frustration experienced by most iPhone users: sending a photo gets stuck, with a blue progress bar perpetually displayed at the top of the screen. Until that photo is finally sent, essentially all subsequent messages get blocked as well.

In iOS 27, this bottleneck has been resolved. Each message has its own progress bar and can be sent independently, so if a photo gets stuck, it won't hold up subsequent text, photo, or video messages.

Finally, iOS 27 improves Messages syncing across devices. Apple says conversations will sync more reliably between different devices, with fewer instances of messages being lost, delayed, or failing to sync when users switch from their iPhone to their Mac.

For a complete look at everything new in the Messages app in iOS 27, click here for our full guide. What do you think of Apple's changes to Messages in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.
